Raamah@Ezk.27.22.description: Raamah was a place, possibly located in Arabia, that traded with the city of Tyre, offering spices, precious stones, and gold.

Raamah@Gen.10.7-1Ch.description: Raamah was a son of Cush, grandson of Ham, and great-grandson of Noah, mentioned in the Table of Nations.

Raamses@Exo.1.11.description: Raamses was one of the store cities built by the Israelites during their enslavement in Egypt, along with Pithom.
Raamses@Exo.1.11.name: Raamses

Rab-mag@Jer.39.3-.description: Rab-mag, a Babylonian official, was present at the capture of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar's army.

Rab-saris@2Ki.18.17.description: Rab-saris was one of the Babylonian officials sent by King Sennacherib to Jerusalem during his campaign against Judah.
Rab-saris@2Ki.18.17.name: Rab-saris

Rab-saris@Jer.39.3-.description: Rab-saris, a Babylonian official, was present at the capture of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar's army.
Rab-saris@Jer.39.3-.name: Rab-saris

Rabbith@Jos.19.20.description: Rabbith was a town in the territory of Issachar, mentioned in the list of cities and towns allocated to the tribe during the division of the Promised Land.
Rabbith@Jos.19.20.name: Rabbith

Rabshakeh@2Ki.18.17-Isa.description: Rabshakeh was a Babylonian official who tried to intimidate Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem into surrendering.
Rabshakeh@2Ki.18.17-Isa.name: Rabshakeh

Raca@Mat.5.22.description: Raca is an Aramaic term of contempt, meaning "empty-headed" or "foolish," which Jesus warned against using to insult others, equating it with murder (<ref="Matthew 5:22">Matthew 5:22</ref>).
Raca@Mat.5.22.name: Raca

Rachel@Gen.29.6-Mat.description: Rachel was the beloved wife of Jacob, and the mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
Rachel@Gen.29.6-Mat.name: Rachel

Raddai@1Ch.2.14.description: Raddai was one of David's brothers, a son of Jesse.
Raddai@1Ch.2.14.name: Raddai

Rahab@Job.9.13-Isa.description: Rahab is a poetic name for Egypt, often represented as a mythical sea monster that God defeated, symbolizing His power over the nations (<ref="Psalm 89:10; Isaiah 51:9">Psalm 89:10; Isaiah 51:9</ref>).
Rahab@Job.9.13-Isa.name: Rahab

Rahab@Jos.2.1-Jas.description: Rahab, a Canaanite woman from Jericho, hid the Israelite spies and was spared during the city's destruction.
Rahab@Jos.2.1-Jas.name: Rahab

Raham@1Ch.2.44.description: Raham was the son of Shema and the father or founder of Jorkeam, from the tribe of Judah.
Raham@1Ch.2.44.name: Raham

Rakem@1Ch.7.16.description: Rakem was a son of Sheresh, from the tribe of Manasseh.
Rakem@1Ch.7.16.name: Rakem

Rakkath@Jos.19.35-Jhn.description: Tiberias (Rakkath), a city on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, near where Jesus fed the five thousand (<ref="Josh. 19:35; Jhn.6.23">Josh. 19:35; Jhn.6.23</ref>).
Rakkath@Jos.19.35-Jhn.name: Rakkath

Rakkon@Jos.19.46.description: Rakkon was a town mentioned in the description of the territory allocated to the tribe of Dan in the Promised Land.
Rakkon@Jos.19.46.name: Rakkon

Ram@1Ch.2.25-.description: Ram was the firstborn son of Jerahmeel, from the tribe of Judah.
Ram@1Ch.2.25-.name: Ram

Ram@Job.32.2.description: Ram was an ancestor of Elihu, one of the men who spoke to Job.
Ram@Job.32.2.name: Ram

Ram@Rut.4.19-Luk.description: Ram was the son of Hezron and an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.
Ram@Rut.4.19-Luk.name: Ram

Ramah@Jos.18.25-Mat.description: Ramah was a town in the territory of Benjamin, often associated with significant events in Israel's history, such as the mourning of Rachel and the imprisonment of Jeremiah.
Ramah@Jos.18.25-Mat.name: Ramah

Ramah@Jos.19.29.description: Ramah was a town located on the border between the territory of Asher and the city-state of Tyre.
Ramah@Jos.19.29.name: Ramah

Ramah@Jos.19.36.description: Ramah was a fortified city located in the territory of Naphtali, mentioned in the list of cities allocated to the tribe during the division of the Promised Land.
Ramah@Jos.19.36.name: Ramah

Ramath-lehi@Jdg.15.17.description: Ramath-lehi, meaning "hill of the jawbone," was the place where Samson killed a thousand Philistines with the jawbone of a donkey.
Ramath-lehi@Jdg.15.17.name: Ramath-lehi

Ramathites@1Ch.27.27.description: The Ramathites were people from Ramah who were in charge of King David's vineyards.
Ramathites@1Ch.27.27.name: Ramathites

Rameses@Gen.47.11-Num.description: Rameses was a city in Egypt where the Israelites lived during their enslavement before the Exodus (<ref="Gen. 47:11; Exo. 12:37">Gen. 47:11; Exo. 12:37</ref>).
Rameses@Gen.47.11-Num.name: Rameses

Ramiah@Ezr.10.25.description: Ramiah was one of the men who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.
Ramiah@Ezr.10.25.name: Ramiah

Ramoth@Gen.31.47-Hos.description: Ramoth, also called Ramoth-gilead, was a city of refuge in Gad and a Levitical city (<ref="Deu. 4:43; Jos. 20:8; 21:38">Deu. 4:43; Jos. 20:8; 21:38</ref>).
Ramoth@Gen.31.47-Hos.name: Ramoth

Rapha@2Sa.21.16-1Ch.description: Rapha was the ancestor of several Philistine giants who fought against David and his mighty warriors.
Rapha@2Sa.21.16-1Ch.name: Rapha

Raphah@1Ch.8.37-.description: Raphah (or Rephaiah) was a son of Binea and a descendant of King Saul.
Raphah@1Ch.8.37-.name: Raphah

Raphu@Num.13.9.description: Raphu was the father of Palti, one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore Canaan.
Raphu@Num.13.9.name: Raphu

Reaiah@1Ch.5.5.description: Reaiah was a Reubenite, the son of Micah, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Reuben.
Reaiah@1Ch.5.5.name: Reaiah

Reaiah@Ezr.2.47-Neh.description: Reaiah was an ancestor of temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile.
Reaiah@Ezr.2.47-Neh.name: Reaiah

Reba@Num.31.8-Jos.description: Reba was one of the five Midianite kings killed by the Israelites during the time of Moses.
Reba@Num.31.8-Jos.name: Reba

Rebekah@Gen.22.23-Rom.description: Rebekah was the wife of Isaac and the mother of Jacob and Esau.
Rebekah@Gen.22.23-Rom.name: Rebekah

Recah@1Ch.4.12.description: Recah was a descendant of Judah through Caleb (<ref="1Ch. 4:12">1Ch. 4:12</ref>).
Recah@1Ch.4.12.name: Recah

Rechab@2Ki.10.15-Jer.description: Rechab was the ancestor of the Rechabites, a nomadic tribe known for their faithfulness to God's commands.
Rechab@2Ki.10.15-Jer.name: Rechab

Rechab@2Sa.4.2-.description: Rechab and his brother Baanah were captains in Ishbosheth's army during the time of David.
Rechab@2Sa.4.2-.name: Rechab

Rechab@Neh.3.14.description: Rechab was the father of Malchijah, who repaired the Dung Gate during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.
Rechab@Neh.3.14.name: Rechab

Red_Sea@Exo.10.19-Heb.description: The Red Sea was the body of water miraculously crossed by the Israelites in their escape from Egypt (<ref="Exo. 13:18; 15:4">Exo. 13:18; 15:4</ref>).
Red_Sea@Exo.10.19-Heb.name: Red_Sea

Reelaiah@Ezr.2.2-Neh.description: Reelaiah (or Raamiah) was one of the leaders who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel after the Babylonian exile.
Reelaiah@Ezr.2.2-Neh.name: Reelaiah

Regem-melech@Zec.7.2.description: Regem-melech was one of the messengers sent to the house of God to inquire of the Lord.
Regem-melech@Zec.7.2.name: Regem-melech

Regem@1Ch.2.47.description: Regem was a son of Jahdai, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
Regem@1Ch.2.47.name: Regem

Rehabiah@1Ch.23.17-.description: Rehabiah was the son of Eliezer and grandson of Moses, a Levite with many descendants.
Rehabiah@1Ch.23.17-.name: Rehabiah

Rehob@2Sa.8.3-.description: Rehob was the father of Hadadezer, the king of Zobah, who was defeated by King David.
Rehob@2Sa.8.3-.name: Rehob

Rehob@Jos.19.28.description: Rehob was a city on the northern border of the territory allotted to the tribe of Asher (<ref="Jos. 19:28">Jos. 19:28</ref>).
Rehob@Jos.19.28.name: Rehob

Rehob@Jos.19.30-1Ch.description: Rehob was a Levitical city within the territory of Asher (<ref="Jos. 19:30; 21:31; 1Ch. 6:75">Jos. 19:30; 21:31; 1Ch. 6:75</ref>).
Rehob@Jos.19.30-1Ch.name: Rehob

Rehob@Neh.10.11.description: Rehob was one of the leaders who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah.
Rehob@Neh.10.11.name: Rehob

Rehoboam@1Ki.11.43-Mat.description: Rehoboam was the son of Solomon and the first king of Judah after the division of the kingdom.
Rehoboam@1Ki.11.43-Mat.name: Rehoboam

Rehoboth@Gen.26.22.description: Rehoboth was the name of a well dug by Isaac where he found room and water (<ref="Gen. 26:22">Gen. 26:22</ref>).
Rehoboth@Gen.26.22.name: Rehoboth

Rehoboth@Gen.36.37-1Ch.description: Rehoboth was a city associated with Shaul, an Edomite king (<ref="Gen. 36:37; 1Ch. 1:48">Gen. 36:37; 1Ch. 1:48</ref>).
Rehoboth@Gen.36.37-1Ch.name: Rehoboth

Rehum@Ezr.2.2-Neh.description: Rehum (or Harim or Nehum) was one of the leaders who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel after the Babylonian exile.
Rehum@Ezr.2.2-Neh.name: Rehum

Rehum@Ezr.4.8-.description: Rehum was a Persian official who wrote to King Artaxerxes, attempting to stop the rebuilding of Jerusalem.
Rehum@Ezr.4.8-.name: Rehum

Rehum@Neh.10.25.description: Rehum was one of the individuals who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah.
Rehum@Neh.10.25.name: Rehum

Rehum@Neh.3.17.description: Rehum was a Levite who helped repair a section of the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.
Rehum@Neh.3.17.name: Rehum

Rei@1Ki.1.8.description: Rei was one of the people who remained loyal to King Solomon during Adonijah's attempt to seize the throne.
Rei@1Ki.1.8.name: Rei

Rekem@1Ch.2.43-.description: Rekem was a son of Hebron, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
Rekem@1Ch.2.43-.name: Rekem

Rekem@Jos.18.27.description: Rekem was a city allotted to the tribe of Benjamin (<ref="Jos. 18:27">Jos. 18:27</ref>).
Rekem@Jos.18.27.name: Rekem

Rekem@Num.31.8-Jos.description: Rekem was one of the five Midianite kings killed by the Israelites during the time of Moses.
Rekem@Num.31.8-Jos.name: Rekem

Remaliah@2Ki.15.25-Isa.description: Remaliah was the father of Pekah, who became king of Israel and reigned for 20 years.
Remaliah@2Ki.15.25-Isa.name: Remaliah

Remeth@Jos.19.21-1Ch.description: Remeth, also called Ramoth, was a Levitical city allotted to the tribe of Issachar (<ref="Jos. 19:21; 1Ch. 6:73">Jos. 19:21; 1Ch. 6:73</ref>).
Remeth@Jos.19.21-1Ch.name: Remeth

Rephael@1Ch.26.7.description: Rephael was one of the gatekeepers of the temple during the reign of King David.
Rephael@1Ch.26.7.name: Rephael

Rephah@1Ch.7.25.description: Rephah was a son of Beriah, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.
Rephah@1Ch.7.25.name: Rephah

Rephaiah@1Ch.3.21.description: Rephaiah was a descendant of King David, mentioned in the genealogy of David's descendants.
Rephaiah@1Ch.3.21.name: Rephaiah

Rephaiah@1Ch.4.42.description: Rephaiah was a Simeonite leader who led an attack against the Amalekites during the time of Hezekiah.
Rephaiah@1Ch.4.42.name: Rephaiah

Rephaiah@1Ch.7.2.description: Rephaiah was a son of Tola, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Issachar.
Rephaiah@1Ch.7.2.name: Rephaiah

Rephaiah@Neh.3.9.description: Rephaiah was the son of Hur and ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, who helped repair a section of the city wall.
Rephaiah@Neh.3.9.name: Rephaiah

Rephaim_Valley@Jos.15.8-Isa.name: Rephaim_Valley

Rephan@Act.7.43.name: Rephan

Rephidim@Exo.17.1-Num.description: Rephidim was a place where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to Sinai (<ref="Exo. 17:1, 8; 19:2; Num. 33:14, 15">Exo. 17:1, 8; 19:2; Num. 33:14, 15</ref>).
Rephidim@Exo.17.1-Num.name: Rephidim

Resen@Gen.10.12.description: Resen was an ancient Assyrian city built by Nimrod between Nineveh and Calah (<ref="Gen. 10:12">Gen. 10:12</ref>).
Resen@Gen.10.12.name: Resen

Resheph@1Ch.7.25.description: Resheph was a son of Beriah, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.
Resheph@1Ch.7.25.name: Resheph

Reu@Gen.11.18-Luk.description: Reu was the son of Peleg and an ancestor of Abraham, living to the age of 239 years.
Reu@Gen.11.18-Luk.name: Reu

Reuben@Gen.29.32-Rev.description: Reuben was the firstborn son of Jacob and Leah, and his descendants formed one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
Reuben@Gen.29.32-Rev.name: Reuben

Reumah@Gen.22.24.description: Reumah was the concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and she bore him four sons.
Reumah@Gen.22.24.name: Reumah

Rezeph@2Ki.19.12-Isa.description: Rezeph was a city conquered by the Assyrians, mentioned in a letter from the Assyrian king to Hezekiah (<ref="2Ki. 19:12; Isa. 37:12">2Ki. 19:12; Isa. 37:12</ref>).

Rezin@2Ki.15.37-Isa.description: Rezin was the king of Aram (Syria) who allied with Pekah, king of Israel, against Ahaz, king of Judah.
Rezin@2Ki.15.37-Isa.name: Rezin

Rezin@Ezr.2.48-Neh.description: Rezin was the ancestor of a family of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned from the Babylonian exile.
Rezin@Ezr.2.48-Neh.name: Rezin

Rezon@1Ki.11.23.description: Rezon, son of Eliada, was an adversary of Solomon who reigned over Aram (Syria) in Damascus.
Rezon@1Ki.11.23.name: Rezon

Rhegium@Act.28.13.description: Rhegium was a city in Italy where Paul's ship stopped on his journey to Rome (<ref="Act. 28:13">Act. 28:13</ref>).
Rhegium@Act.28.13.name: Rhegium

Rhesa@Luk.3.27.description: Rhesa was the son of Zerubbabel and an ancestor of Jesus Christ, according to Luke's genealogy.
Rhesa@Luk.3.27.name: Rhesa

Rhoda@Act.12.13.name: Rhoda

Rhodes@Act.21.1.description: Rhodes was an island where Paul stopped during his journey to Jerusalem (<ref="Act. 21:1">Act. 21:1</ref>).
Rhodes@Act.21.1.name: Rhodes

Ribai@2Sa.23.29-1Ch.description: Ribai was the father of Ittai the Gibeathite, one of David's mighty men.
Ribai@2Sa.23.29-1Ch.name: Ribai

Riblah@2Ki.23.33-Ezk.description: Riblah was a city in Hamath where the Babylonians set up their headquarters during their campaigns against Judah (<ref="2Ki. 23:33; 25:6, 20-21; Jer. 39:5-6; 52:9-10, 26-27">2Ki. 23:33; 25:6, 20-21; Jer. 39:5-6; 52:9-10, 26-27</ref>).
Riblah@2Ki.23.33-Ezk.name: Riblah

Riblah@Num.34.11.description: Riblah was a place mentioned in the description of the eastern border of the Promised Land (<ref="Num. 34:11">Num. 34:11</ref>).
Riblah@Num.34.11.name: Riblah

Rimmon-perez@Num.33.19-.description: Rimmon-perez was a place where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to Canaan (<ref="Num. 33:19-20">Num. 33:19-20</ref>).
Rimmon-perez@Num.33.19-.name: Rimmon-perez

Rimmon@2Ki.5.18.description: Rimmon was a Syrian deity worshipped by Naaman, who asked for God's pardon for bowing down in Rimmon's temple (<ref="2Ki.5.18">2Ki.5.18</ref>).
Rimmon@2Ki.5.18.name: Rimmon

Rimmon@2Sa.4.2-.description: Rimmon was a Beerothite and the father of Rechab and Baanah, who murdered Ish-bosheth, Saul's son.
Rimmon@2Sa.4.2-.name: Rimmon

Rimmon@Jdg.20.45-.description: Rimmon was a rock where 600 Benjamite survivors fled after a battle with the other Israelite tribes (<ref="Jdg. 20:45, 47; 21:13">Jdg. 20:45, 47; 21:13</ref>).
Rimmon@Jdg.20.45-.name: Rimmon

Rimmon@Jos.15.32-1Ch.description: Rimmon, a town allotted to Judah and later given to Simeon, was located in the Negev region.
Rimmon@Jos.15.32-1Ch.name: Rimmon

Rinnah@1Ch.4.20.description: Rinnah was a son of Shimon, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
Rinnah@1Ch.4.20.name: Rinnah

Riphath@Gen.10.3-1Ch.description: Riphath was a son of Gomer and grandson of Japheth, mentioned in the Table of Nations.
Riphath@Gen.10.3-1Ch.name: Riphath

Rissah@Num.33.21-.description: Rissah was a place where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to Canaan (<ref="Num. 33:21-22">Num. 33:21-22</ref>).
Rissah@Num.33.21-.name: Rissah

Rithmah@Num.33.18-.description: Rithmah was a place where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to Canaan (<ref="Num. 33:18-19">Num. 33:18-19</ref>).
Rithmah@Num.33.18-.name: Rithmah

Rizia@1Ch.7.39.description: Rizia was a son of Ulla, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.
Rizia@1Ch.7.39.name: Rizia

Rizpah@2Sa.3.7-.description: Rizpah was a concubine of King Saul and the mother of Armoni and Mephibosheth, who were executed by the Gibeonites.
Rizpah@2Sa.3.7-.name: Rizpah

Rock_of_Escape@1Sa.23.28.description: The Rock of Escape was a place where Saul stopped pursuing David after being called away to fight the Philistines (<ref="1Sa. 23:28">1Sa. 23:28</ref>).
Rock_of_Escape@1Sa.23.28.name: Rock_of_Escape

Rogelim@2Sa.17.27-.description: Rogelim was the hometown of Barzillai the Gileadite, who provided supplies for David during Absalom's rebellion (<ref="2Sa. 17:27; 19:31">2Sa. 17:27; 19:31</ref>).
Rogelim@2Sa.17.27-.name: Rogelim

Rohgah@1Ch.7.34.description: Rohgah was a son of Shomer (or 'Shamer'), mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.
Rohgah@1Ch.7.34.name: Rohgah

Romamti-ezer@1Ch.25.4-.description: Romamti-ezer was a son of Heman and a Levitical singer during the reign of King David.
Romamti-ezer@1Ch.25.4-.name: Romamti-ezer

Rome@Jhn.11.48-Phm.description: Rome was the capital of the Roman Empire, where Paul was imprisoned and wrote several epistles (<ref="Act.28.16; Rom. 1:7">Act.28.16; Rom. 1:7</ref>).
Rome@Jhn.11.48-Phm.name: Rome

Rosh@Gen.46.21-1Ch.description: Rosh (or Rapha) was a son of Benjamin and grandson of Jacob, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.
Rosh@Gen.46.21-1Ch.name: Rosh

Rufus@Mrk.15.21.description: Rufus was the son of Simon of Cyrene, who was compelled to carry Jesus' cross on the way to His crucifixion.
Rufus@Mrk.15.21.name: Rufus

Rufus@Rom.16.13.name: Rufus

Ruth@Rut.1.4-Mat.description: Ruth was a Moabite woman who married Boaz and became an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.
Ruth@Rut.1.4-Mat.name: Ruth
